diagnoses.label: amount_tier_last_candidate_without_backoff_on_parse_failure
diagnoses.general_pattern: When a priority-tier keyword matches multiple lines and the LAST matching line fails numeric parsing (non-decimal 'count' value, OCR-corrupted digits, or empty keyword line), the pipeline silently falls through to a next-line fallback or returns None instead of walking back to earlier same-tier candidates that have a cleanly parseable monetary token.
diagnoses.wrong_approach: Algorithm picks `candidates[-1]`, runs `extract_last_number` once, and if that returns None, consults only the next 1-2 physical lines (which may be a GST-summary tax column) rather than iterating remaining same-tier candidates in reverse order.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: In 074.jpg the TOTAL tier matched both the misspelled 'Toial Amt Rounded' context and 'Total Item(s): 4'; because 'Total Item(s): 4' has no decimal, fallback grabbed 96.23 from the subsequent 'SR ... 96.23' GST-summary line (think log m0027). In 077.jpg two TOTAL tier candidates exist ('Total (Inclusive of GST): 23.26' and 'TOTAL: 23.25'); the last-only policy selected the OCR-corrupted 23.25 instead of the corroborated 23.26. In 078.jpg amount came out as empty string, consistent with a tier yielding a None value that was then written as '' rather than Python None.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: Within a tier, iterate accepted candidates from last to first and return the first one whose own text yields a two-decimal monetary token; only consult a split-line fallback when the keyword line contains zero digits, and only against pre-cutoff, non-exclusion, non-payment lines (as the receipt_total_keyword_priority_disambiguation anchor already prescribes).
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Collect all non-excluded same-tier candidates, reverse-iterate, require a two-decimal match on the keyword line itself before accepting; use next-line fallback only when the keyword line is digit-free and the next line is itself pre-cutoff and not payment/tender; fall through to the next tier only when every candidate in the current tier is exhausted.
diagnoses.scope_boundary: Receipt-style OCR tasks that declare an explicit priority tier list plus an exclusion list and require a two-decimal monetary string; applies when a single tier can match multiple lines in the same receipt.
diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: Non-receipt OCR, free-form text extraction, or tasks where only one keyword line is expected per receipt; do not use to override a strictly higher-priority tier.
diagnoses.target_section: Structured Field Extraction from Receipts → Mechanism anchor: receipt_total_keyword_priority_disambiguation

diagnoses.label: gst_tax_summary_cutoff_not_enforced_before_last_candidate_selection
diagnoses.general_pattern: Lines appearing after a 'GST SUMMARY'/'TAX SUMMARY'/tax-table header reuse the words 'Total'/'Amount' as column labels and should be ineligible as monetary total candidates, but the current executor only applies exclusion patterns to individual lines and does not track a section-level cutoff index.
diagnoses.wrong_approach: Per-line regex exclusion catches 'GST Summary' or 'Tax Code' lines themselves but still admits subsequent 'Total:', 'a Total', or 'SR ... <amount> ...' lines as tier candidates.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: In 074.jpg the trailing 'SR gy a% 96.23 B77' line (post 'GST Summary Amount (RM) Tax (RM)') was reachable via next-line fallback and produced 96.23. In 034.jpg (ok on amount here but conceptually at risk) and in 071.jpg trajectory discussion (think log m0027), post-'GST Summary' 'Total 16.71 0.99' was identified as a prior failure mode where 0.99 was picked. The run also records a pre-cutoff reasoning gap in m0027.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: Scan once for a 'GST SUMMARY'/'TAX SUMMARY'/'SST SUMMARY' or tax-table column-header pattern, record its line index, and treat all later lines as ineligible for every tier (both direct match and split-line fallback).
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Compute `summary_cutoff` on normalized text; filter the candidate pool to indices < cutoff before tier matching; apply the same filter to the next-line fallback target.
diagnoses.scope_boundary: Receipts that print a tax/GST/SST summary table or tax-code column after the payment block.
diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: Receipts without a tax summary section; non-receipt documents; cases where the only 'Total' line truly lives after a summary header (none observed in this family).
diagnoses.target_section: Structured Field Extraction from Receipts → Mechanism anchor: receipt_total_keyword_priority_disambiguation (step 2 'Detect a summary-section cutoff')

diagnoses.label: ocr_digit_confusable_substitution_not_applied_on_total_tokens
diagnoses.general_pattern: Tesseract substitutes letters for digits inside monetary tokens on receipt-tier lines (u/o/O→0, l/I→1, S→5, B→8, Z→2), producing tokens like '15.u00' or truncated 'XX.X' that the strict two-decimal regex rejects, causing the amount cell to be written as null even though the surrounding line clearly matched a tier keyword.
diagnoses.wrong_approach: The executor applies no normalization inside the amount token and relies solely on a strict `\d+\.\d{2}` regex, so any letter-for-digit confusion yields a parse failure and null is written.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: In 011.jpg OCR produced 'TOTAL 15.u00' and the extractor returned None for a receipt that cleanly matched a GRAND TOTAL/TOTAL tier (think log m0027). The run also recorded 077.jpg/083.jpg/094.jpg initially returning None for similar reasons before PSM switching; final output still shows 078.jpg total_amount='' and 077.jpg total_amount='23.26' versus 23.25 anchor ambiguity.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: On a line that matched a total-tier keyword, apply a bounded confusables substitution restricted to tokens already dominated by digits and separators, then re-apply the two-decimal regex; never apply the substitution to free text, product names, GST IDs, or dates.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Add a token-scoped normalization pass before the monetary regex on tier-matched lines; keep it off by default elsewhere; reject one-decimal matches as OCR truncation and back off to an earlier same-tier candidate (per the two-decimal invariant anchor).
diagnoses.scope_boundary: Receipt tasks with the two-decimal monetary invariant; only on tier-matched lines; only within tokens whose character class is already numeric-dominant.
diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: Invoice numbers, phone numbers, GST IDs, dates, product codes, or any numeric field that is not the receipt total.
diagnoses.target_section: Structured Field Extraction from Receipts → Mechanism anchor: ocr_amount_normalization_and_arithmetic_crosscheck

diagnoses.label: null_vs_empty_string_writeback_regression
diagnoses.general_pattern: Task contract requires failed extractions to be written as null, but the writeback stage emits an empty string for at least one cell, producing a cell whose `cell.value == ""` rather than `cell.value is None`.
diagnoses.wrong_approach: The extraction function appears to return a formatted string (likely `f"{val:.2f}"` or `""`) rather than Python `None` when parsing fails, and the assignment path routes that string straight into openpyxl.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: In the delivered xlsx row for 078.jpg, total_amount is the empty string `""` instead of null, while 063/078 field feedback shows amount_correct=false for 078.jpg; other rows carry two-decimal strings as required. Trajectory shows no verification pass that reloads the workbook to assert `cell.value is None`.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: Return Python `None` from the extraction function on failure, assign it directly to the openpyxl cell (never through `str()`/`f-string`), and verify on reload that failed cells satisfy `cell.value is None`.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Keep a strict None sentinel through the pipeline, add a post-save `load_workbook(path, data_only=True)` self-check that asserts null-vs-empty and the two-decimal format before `finish`.
diagnoses.scope_boundary: Tasks whose contract explicitly distinguishes null from empty string in output cells (data-only extraction xlsx).
diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: Tasks where `""` is an acceptable sentinel, formatted financial models with formula outputs, or tasks that mandate a specific placeholder string.
diagnoses.target_section: Preserving null vs empty string on writeback / Delivery contract verification for data-only xlsx outputs

diagnoses.label: date_label_binding_vs_first_date_regex_match_on_ambiguous_batches
diagnoses.general_pattern: When a receipt contains multiple date-like tokens (transaction date, print timestamp, closed date, loyalty/promo date) and the dominant batch locale is DD/MM/YYYY, taking the first regex match or applying MM/DD-style parsing produces a mis-bound ISO date.
diagnoses.wrong_approach: The executor iterates DATE_PATTERNS over lines and returns the first calendar-valid tuple as (d, m, y) without checking the surrounding label (DATE / INVOICE DATE / DATA) or filtering out PRINT/CLOSED/FRN/LOYALTY/PROMO contexts.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: For 034.jpg, OCR shows 'Date: 09/03/2018' on the receipt, which under DD/MM/YYYY is 2018-03-09; the delivered row records 2018-08-09, consistent with a MM/DD/YYYY interpretation of 09/03/2018 or binding to a different date token. Field feedback marks only 034.jpg date_correct=false while 21/22 other rows pass, consistent with a locale-binding edge case rather than global failure.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: Prefer date lines whose canonicalized text contains DATE/INVOICE DATE (or OCR variants DATA/DAIE) and are not prefixed by PRINT/CLOSED/CLOSING/FRN/LOYALTY/PROMO; parse under declared locale (Malaysian receipts: DD/MM/YYYY primary) and only fall back to other orderings when unambiguous rows in the batch justify it.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Bind the extracted date to a label and the task-declared locale before emitting ISO; infer dominant ordering from unambiguous rows (first component >12) and never override an unambiguous row by batch majority.
diagnoses.scope_boundary: Receipt tasks with multiple date-like tokens per image or a declared national locale.
diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: Single-date documents, non-receipt OCR, or tasks that explicitly declare a different locale.
diagnoses.target_section: Structured Field Extraction from Receipts → Mechanism anchor: receipt_date_label_binding_and_locale

diagnoses.label: iteration_budget_exhausted_by_image_by_image_debug_loop
diagnoses.general_pattern: The source agent consumed the parent iteration budget (65/65, termination_reason=max_iterations) in an interactive per-image debug loop (repeated OCR dumps, preprocessing trials, think-tool monologues) instead of running one diagnostic pass followed by a consolidated edit and a single re-run.
diagnoses.wrong_approach: Trajectory shows 27 terminal + 22 think + 16 file_editor calls, with sequential image-by-image OCR exploration (m0003..m0045 window) before converging on a pipeline, then hitting the iteration cap during consolidation.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: execution_metadata.agent_iterations=65 at max_iterations, acp_stop_reason='max_turn_requests', 22 think calls indicating long inner reasoning monologues per image, and request/response growth across 15+ exchanges before the extraction script even existed (first file_editor create at m0021).
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: For batch OCR over N images, run a single diagnostic pass that dumps per-image per-variant OCR slices, candidate tuples, and current predictions; plan one consolidated set of pattern/variant edits; re-run once; only then enter targeted debugging.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Adopt the batch-diagnostic-then-batch-edit workflow explicitly, keep interactive think-tool usage proportional to novel evidence, and avoid re-OCRing images that already have stable text.
diagnoses.scope_boundary: Batch extraction tasks with N≥10 similar inputs under a bounded iteration budget.
diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: Single-image tasks, tasks where each image legitimately needs bespoke handling, or tasks without an iteration cap.
diagnoses.target_section: Structured Field Extraction from Receipts → Workflow note: batch-diagnostic-then-batch-edit

overlay.composition_issue: The current image-ocr receipt overlay already names the right anchors (keyword priority, two-decimal invariant, amount normalization, null-vs-empty), but the executor's implementation of 'take the last same-tier candidate' is weaker than the anchor's step 3c, which requires reverse-iteration until a two-decimal match is found and bars next-line fallback when the keyword line contains digits. The GST/TAX summary cutoff (step 2) is also under-enforced — exclusion is per-line only, not section-level. Finally, the null-vs-empty writeback contract in xlsx/SKILL.md is present but was not verified on reload for the 078.jpg cell. These three gaps compose: a weak tier-walk interacts with a missing summary cutoff to let post-summary numbers leak in, and a missing writeback self-check lets an empty-string cell ship. Strengthening the three anchors (and keeping their negative boundaries intact) addresses all observed Skill-controllable amount failures without reopening generic OCR behavior.
preservation_constraints: Do not expand receipt-specific hints into openai-vision, pdf, video-frame-extraction, or generic xlsx guidance.
Preserve the explicit scope line that the receipt overlay only applies when the task declares its own keyword/exclusion/null conventions.
Preserve the two-decimal invariant's rejection of one-decimal padding; do not silently pad OCR truncations.
Preserve the negative boundaries on OCR-confusables substitution (only inside digit-dominant tokens on tier-matched lines; never on IDs/phones/dates).
Preserve the null-vs-empty rule as scoped to data-only extraction contracts; do not apply it to tasks where '' is acceptable.
Preserve the batch-diagnostic-then-batch-edit note as workflow guidance, not a hard constraint on single-image tasks.
Do not introduce task-specific expected values, oracle amounts, or hard-coded per-filename repairs.

package_assessment.rationale: All six diagnosed failures map onto reusable mechanism anchors that already exist (or are naturally located) in the current image-ocr and xlsx SKILL.md files: tier-walk disambiguation, GST/TAX summary cutoff, two-decimal invariant + confusables normalization, label-bound date parsing, null-vs-empty writeback, and batch-diagnostic workflow. The failures are observable in the trajectory and delivered xlsx (think logs m0018/m0027/m0033/m0039/m0045, 22-row output, 078.jpg empty amount, 034.jpg mis-bound date) without needing hidden oracle values. The run terminated at the iteration cap with a persistent-skill executor, so the executor itself is operational; the gaps are in Skill guidance strength and composition rather than infrastructure. No infra_or_executor_only defects were identified.
